analysis.title: Tactical asset allocation, November 2026
key_insights: Invesco's framework stays in a slowdown regime for the seventh consecutive month. Global growth is above trend while global risk appetite is decelerating.

Invesco's global leading economic indicator (LEI) has been above trend for 10 consecutive months. The LEI rose in eight of the nine month-to-month comparisons after the first reading of the streak, the highest share among the eight historical streaks since 1988.
Higher global yields and tighter financial conditions have begun to challenge growth expectations tied to the AI buildout and the earnings level relative to the price multiple.

The AI momentum-trade unwind was most visible in emerging market equities. South Korea, China and Taiwan (~64% of the index weight) fell -18%, -7% and -3%. US technology-heavy indexes also came under pressure.

Credit stress is building at the bottom of the quality range. The spread gap between CCC-rated debt and the broader high yield benchmark keeps widening, near levels last seen in 2020, 2016 and 2008. Broad high yield spreads remain tight.
Third-quarter earnings are strong in absolute terms but are being challenged on a relative basis, because a historic level of growth is already priced into multiples this year.

Inflation momentum remains elevated, led by global energy prices. Oil freight costs have risen sharply, which could keep refined product prices (gasoline, diesel, heating oil) high even if benchmark crude stabilizes.

In October the 10-year real yield fell 27 basis points from its September peak. Treasuries returned 2.4% and the S&P 500 fell 0.9%. Since 2002, in the 35 months with a real yield drop of at least 25 bps, Treasuries averaged 2.1%.
When equities fell and real yields dropped at least 25 bps, Treasuries were positive 94% of the time and outperformed equities every time. Invesco treats duration as a hedge against slowing growth.

Positioning is risk-neutral versus benchmark with a moderate overweight to equities over fixed income, tilted to defensive factors (quality, low volatility) and defensive sectors (select technology, health care, consumer staples) over cyclicals.

Regionally Invesco prefers the US over developed ex-US markets, and developed over emerging markets. Emerging markets and China are in a contraction regime, while emerging markets ex-China are in slowdown.
In fixed income Invesco holds a moderate underweight to credit and an overweight to duration, preferring inflation-linked bonds.

Currency stance: neutral USD. Underweight AUD, GBP, NZD, SEK and CHF. Overweight CAD, EUR, JPY, NOK and SGD. In emerging markets, overweight INR, IDR, MYR, TWD and THB, funded by underweights in COP, CZK, MXN and ZAR.
Invesco cites geopolitical risk and political uncertainty ahead of the US midterm elections as reasons for diversification and prudent risk-taking.

tension_points.bull_case: Global growth is above trend, the LEI streak has been unusually consistent, and Q3 earnings are strong in absolute terms.
tension_points.bear_case: Higher yields and tighter financial conditions challenge AI-buildout growth expectations, earnings are challenged relative to multiples, and CCC spreads are widening.
tension_points.what_invalidates: If tighter financial conditions weaken growth and pull real rates lower, duration would outperform equities, as it did in October.
